task.description:
Review the Step 2a implementation (commit 9ac7c2eb on branch feature/WF02-batch-4-20260811) against docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md. This batch touches: (1) src/db/partition_conversion.zig -- PAR-05 online partition conversion, a schema/DDL-adjacent operation on the events table; (2) migrations/1150_par06_instance_projections_event_window.sql -- PAR-06 window-column migration plus Store.append()/reconstructBounded() changes; (3) src/engine/pin_resolver.zig -- PIN-01 AC3/AC4/AC5, resolves variable_schema and applies pin_overrides, returns UnresolvedCatalogRef/UnresolvedModuleRef for the explicitly out-of-scope AC1/AC2 branches; (4) migrations/1151_pin02_instance_started_pinned_versions.sql and the src/engine/instance.zig InstanceStore.create() call site -- PIN-02, pin set now recorded in the INSTANCE_STARTED event payload. Determine independently whether any of this is a tenant-data path (new/changed API route, migration, Lua/Wasm host function, secrets code, or response-shaping/lookup-by-ID code) requiring full review against the numbered security invariants, or whether it is out of scope for a PASS-with-note. Do not assume the answer -- this is your determination to make, not ORCH's. Pay particular attention to: tenant isolation in the partition-conversion backfill/swap path (PAR-05), whether the new window columns/migration in PAR-06 could leak cross-tenant data through reconstruction, and whether PIN-01/PIN-02's variable_schema and pin_overrides resolution paths enforce tenant scoping when looking up catalog/schema entries by reference.

REWORK 1 RE-REVIEW: BACKEND-DEV fixed the INV-1 finding in commit 23eff3b2. pin_resolver.zig's
resolveServiceCatalogRef() now binds tenant_id as a parameterized $2::uuid against
service_catalog.owner_tenant_id (threaded via ResolutionInput.tenant_id, sourced in instance.zig
from the existing threadlocal tenant_context populated by auth middleware), replacing the dropped
bpm_effective_tenant_id() SQL function reference entirely. New regression test
tests/integration/pin01_service_catalog_tenant_scope_test.zig (3 cases: cross-tenant denial via
UnresolvedCatalogRef, same-tenant success, global-scope success) verified passing 3/3 against real
Postgres via the new test-integration-pin01 build step. Please re-review specifically:
1. Confirm the ::uuid binding in resolveServiceCatalogRef() (pin_resolver.zig, near line 197) is
   correctly parameterized (no string interpolation) and correctly scopes by owner_tenant_id.
2. Confirm tenant_id in instance.zig is sourced from a trustworthy request-scoped context (not
   client-supplied, not guessable) -- verify tenant_context.get() is populated only by auth
   middleware from the validated JWT/session, not from any request body/query param.
3. Confirm the regression test genuinely proves cross-tenant denial (not just a same-tenant happy
   path) by reading tests/integration/pin01_service_catalog_tenant_scope_test.zig directly.
4. PAR-05 and PAR-06 do not need re-review -- unchanged since your original PASS.


REWORK 2 RE-REVIEW (post Step 3 TEST-DESIGNER + two further BACKEND-DEV rework cycles,
commits 0d123515, 29314c89, 01d9f6a3): after your REWORK 1 PASS (commit 39d13534),
TEST-DESIGNER (Step 3) wrote real integration tests that exposed 4 correctness BLOCKER
defects in this run's own PAR-05/PAR-06/PIN-01 code, which were routed back to BACKEND-DEV
as in-run rework (not deferred, since they were this run's own code failing this run's own
new tests against this run's own MUST ACs) and are now fixed across two further rework
commits:

1. commit 29314c89 (rework 2):
   - PAR-05: src/db/partition_conversion.zig PartitionConverter.createParent() now adds
     ALTER TABLE events_part ADD PRIMARY KEY (event_id, created_at) after the LIKE-based
     CREATE TABLE (ISS-0676/GH-718).
   - PAR-06: src/engine/instance.zig gained a new bumpEventWindowInTx() helper, called after
     all 7 transaction-terminal UPDATE instance_projections statements covering all 12 raw
     INSERT INTO events call sites, to maintain first_event_at/last_event_at (ISS-0677/GH-719).
   - PIN-01 AC3: src/engine/pin_resolver.zig validateVariableSchema() now wraps scalar field
     values/schemas in synthetic one-key objects before calling
     registry.validatePayloadAgainstSchema() (ISS-0679/GH-721).
2. commit 01d9f6a3 (rework 3, FINAL -- rework budget for Step 2a is now exhausted at 3/3):
   - PAR-05: src/scheduler/partition_maintenance.zig gained a new shared
     upsertPartitionCatalogRow() helper (factored out of ensurePartitionAttached()).
     src/db/partition_conversion.zig backfillOneMonth() now calls it after each
     attachPartitionTimed(); swap() now updates plat_partition_catalog.parent_table at
     rename time in the same transaction; reconcileOrRollback() was restructured to drive
     its mismatch-detection loop from the new side's own catalog rows and a new
     countRowsInRange() helper bounding a COUNT(*) against events_legacy (ISS-0681/GH-724).

Please re-review specifically:
1. PAR-05's DDL/backfill/swap/reconcile path (src/db/partition_conversion.zig,
   src/scheduler/partition_maintenance.zig) -- this is schema/DDL-adjacent, your original
   scope. Confirm the new plat_partition_catalog upsert and the restructured
   reconcileOrRollback()/countRowsInRange() do not introduce any tenant-isolation gap (is
   plat_partition_catalog itself tenant-scoped or global/platform-level? if global, confirm
   no cross-tenant data is exposed by the new bookkeeping) and that the parameterized query
   discipline (no string interpolation) holds in the new/changed SQL.
2. PAR-06's src/engine/instance.zig bumpEventWindowInTx() and its 7 call sites -- confirm
   this is purely mechanical window-column maintenance (no new tenant-scoping surface,
   no new lookup-by-ID path) and does not touch or weaken the INV-1 tenant-scoping fix you
   already verified in REWORK 1 re-review (commit 23eff3b2) for resolveServiceCatalogRef()/
   instance.zig's tenant_context threading -- confirm via diff that this rework's hunks are
   disjoint from that code.
3. PIN-01 AC3's validateVariableSchema() change -- confirm the synthetic object-wrapping
   is purely a payload-shape adaptation (no new external input trusted without validation,
   no SQL/eval injection surface) and does not touch resolveServiceCatalogRef() or any
   tenant-scoped lookup.
4. Confirm no NEW SERVICE_TASK/tenant-scoped resolution code was added anywhere in this
   rework sequence beyond what REWORK 1 already reviewed.

PASS with these specific confirmations, or FAIL naming the exact invariant number and
file:line if something is wrong. Any NEW incidental security-adjacent finding is filed as
its own ISS + GitHub issue per core-directives.md, not silently noted only in this handoff.


REWORK 3 RE-REVIEW (post Step 3b TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR FAIL + BACKEND-DEV fix, handoff
e0439a14-f763-4e97-b2a4-b4250e455f81, commit 51583e25): TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (Step 3b)

comments corrected, and ISS-0682/GH-725 (a test-fixture casing bug) was fixed and closed as a
bonus.

Please re-review specifically:
1. src/engine/pin_resolver.zig's applyOverrideToPins() and applyPinOverrides() diff (use
   git diff 99fbc164..51583e25 -- src/engine/pin_resolver.zig) -- confirm this is purely a

2. Confirm the fix does not introduce a NEW leak or use-after-free on any path (e.g. confirm

   including the pre-existing error paths already tracked as ISS-0680/GH-722).
3. Confirm no NEW SERVICE_TASK/tenant-scoped resolution code was added.

result.summary: REWORK 3 (FINAL) re-review PASS. Independently re-reviewed commit 51583e25 (git diff 99fbc164..51583e25 -- src/engine/pin_resolver.zig) fixing ISS-0683/GH-727 (double-free/Invalid free on PIN-01 AC4 happy path). (1) Confirmed pure memory-lifetime fix: applyOverrideToPins() (pin_resolver.zig:563-580) now takes allocator and allocator.dupe()s resolved_id/version before storing into the pin, freeing the pin's old resolved_id/version (:571-572) before overwrite; both call sites (:504-520 catalog_entry, :526-543 variable_schema) now unconditionally defer-free their own resolved/current copies (:513-514, :534-536). Diff touches only lines 503-580 (applyPinOverrides/applyOverrideToPins) -- confirmed disjoint via line-range comparison against REWORK 1 (resolveServiceCatalogRef, lines 219-262, untouched since commit 23eff3b2) and REWORK 2 (validateVariableSchema, ~line 375-452, untouched by this diff per `git diff 99fbc164..51583e25` hunk headers at lines 503/517/530 only). No SQL, no catch unreachable, no new query text introduced (grep on the diff confirms). (2) Confirmed no new leak/UAF: traced full lifecycle -- Step 2/3 populates pins.items with allocator-owned resolved_id/version; Step 5 (applyPinOverrides, still operating on pins.items) either leaves a pin untouched or applyOverrideToPins() frees the original and installs a fresh dupe; Step 6 cleanup loop (lines 160-196, pre-existing, unchanged) dupes into the final owned[] slice and frees pins.items[i].resolved_id/.version exactly once regardless of override outcome -- single ownership throughout, no alias downstream (instance.zig only consumes the final owned[] return value, confirmed via grep -- this diff does not touch instance.zig at all). Independently ran `zig build test-integration-pin01` against real Postgres (BPM_TEST_DB_URL) twice with different seeds: both runs report 9/9 tests passed, 0 crashes, 0 Invalid free panics, matching BACKEND-DEV's own verification; TC-PIN-01-03 (the AC4 accepting-path test that previously crashed with the double-free) now passes cleanly both times. Build step reports 8 pre-existing leaks in both runs -- these are ISS-0680/GH-722 (OPEN, MAJOR, error-path-only leaks confined to TC-PIN-01-02/-04, an unrelated pre-existing issue, correctly out of scope per this rework task and untouched by this fix). (3) Confirmed no new SERVICE_TASK/tenant-scoped resolution code added: diff contains zero new pub fn, zero new SQL, zero new call into resolveServiceCatalogRef() or any tenant-scoped lookup -- only allocator.dupe/allocator.free calls and comments. No new incidental security-adjacent finding surfaced during this review.
